front.title: Gerarion Universal Standard (GUS) 2.1: Regular Calendar, Continuous Instant and Post-Quantum Verifiable Signed Time

abstract.t: This document specifies the Gerarion Universal Standard (GUS) version 2.1: a regular civil calendar (12 months of exactly 30 days plus a Tempalum closing period of 4 or 11 days), an invariant week (every year lasts exactly 52 or 53 weeks, so any given date always falls on the same weekday), a continuous count of seconds (no leap seconds), a canonical timestamp format, and a signed timestamp (GST) verifiable with stateless hash-based (quantum-resistant) signatures and a chained notary. The time value is designed so that forging a valid timestamp costs more than any benefit it can produce.

note.title: Requirements Language
note.t: The key words "MUST", "MUST NOT", "REQUIRED", "SHALL", "SHALL NOT", "SHOULD", "SHOULD NOT", "RECOMMENDED", "NOT RECOMMENDED", "MAY", and "OPTIONAL" in this document are to be interpreted as described in BCP 14 when, and only when, they appear in all capitals, as shown here.

section.title: Introduction
section.t: Time on most computers is expressed in calendars with irregular months, mobile weekdays, leap seconds, and political rewinding. None of those properties is arithmetic: they are conventions that can be altered by decree, misconfigured hosts, or hostile reconfiguration. GUS 2.1 replaces the calendar substrate with an exact integer system and wraps the resulting value in signatures and notarization, so that the time itself becomes an auditable fact rather than a host configuration.

GUS 2.1 replaces the internal corpus GERO-1.2 (a historical draft never registered in the IETF datatracker). All divergences from that corpus are recorded in the errata document of the specification repository.

section.title: Calendar structure
section.t: The GUS calendar consists of a regular block of 12 months × 30 days (360 days), followed by a closing period named Tempalum (month 00) of 4 days in common years and 11 days in Great Tempalum (GT) years. A common year is exactly 364 days (52 weeks); a GT year is exactly 371 days (53 weeks). Therefore a given GUS date falls on the same weekday every year: implementations MUST NOT introduce any day whose index breaks this invariant.

The sequence of GT years is defined by an exact integer recurrence (the solar accumulator), with no floating point arithmetic: year n is GT if and only if r(n) + 1242190 ≥ 7000000, where r(0) = 0 and r(n) = r(n-1) + 1242190 - (7000000 if the previous step saturated). Implementations MUST use integer arithmetic and MUST NOT reproduce the GT sequence by any other approximation, including floating point.

The origin is day index 0 = 1 Keuphero of year 0 DY = Julian Day Number 1719313. That value is the only normative anchor of the system. Any translation to a civil calendar (for example, the proleptic Gregorian date of the origin) is a derived result of exact arithmetic and MUST NOT be used as an input of the algorithm.

section.title: Continuous instant
section.t: The GUS instant is a signed integer number of seconds since the origin (day 0, 00:00:00). Days are always exactly 86400 seconds; GUS time MUST NOT apply leap seconds (analogous to TAI). For any day index d and time-of-day (h, m, s): instant = d × 86400 + h×3600 + m×60 + s, with 0 ≤ h ≤ 23, 0 ≤ m ≤ 59, 0 ≤ s ≤ 59. The luminous cycle label is semantic only: SC = 06:00-17:59 and LC = 18:00-05:59; it MUST NOT alter arithmetic.

section.title: Canonical timestamp format
section.t: The canonical timestamp format is:
section.sourcecode: gero-stamp = gero-date [ gero-time ] gero-date = 1*4DIGIT era "-" month "-" day "-" weekday era = "DY" / "AY" month = 2DIGIT ; 00 = Tempalum, 01..12 regular day = 2DIGIT ; 1..30, or 1..4/1..11 in Tempalum weekday = %x53 / %x4C / %x4D / %x41 / %x54 / %x56 / %x42 gero-time = "-" hms "-" cycle gero-offset hms = 2DIGIT ":" 2DIGIT ":" 2DIGIT ; 00..23 : 00..59 : 00..59 cycle = "SC" / "LC" gero-offset = "TCJ" ("+" / "-") 1*2DIGIT
section.t: Parsers SHOULD accept, and emitters MUST NOT emit, the following relaxations: '.' in place of '-' as separators, single spaces in place of separators, case-insensitive era and weekday letters, era omitted (defaults to DY), and up to 4 digits in the year. Parsers MUST reject hour values above 23 and minute/second values above 59; the optional time block is atomic: parsers MUST NOT accept a partial time block (for example, hours without the TCJ offset).

The declared weekday letter and the declared cycle are advisory: the computed weekday and cycle always prevail. A conforming parser either silently corrects them and raises a "weekday_corrected" / "cycle_corrected" flag, or (strict mode) rejects with GERO_EWEEK if the weekday letter is inconsistent. The day-letter conflicts of calendars with mobile weeks do not exist in GUS: the weekday is day_index mod 7 by definition.

Error codes: GERO_EINVAL (malformed syntax or field out of range), GERO_ETEMPALUM (Tempalum day that does not exist in that year type), GERO_EWEEK (strict-weekday mismatch). A Tempalum day above 4 in a common year or above 11 in a GT year MUST raise GERO_ETEMPALUM.

section.title: Signed timestamp (GST)
section.t: A GST (Gerarion Signed Timestamp) is a JSON document with fields v (format version, currently 2), ctx (domain-separation constant, "GUS2-TS"), alg (signature algorithm name), ts (canonical stamp), ins (continuous instant), day (day index), pub (public key as hex), sig (signature) and optional anchor (notary inclusion proof).

The bytes to sign MUST be exactly: ctx || "
" || ts || "
" || ins || "
" in UTF-8.

Production deployments SHOULD use stateless hash-based signatures standardized in FIPS 205 (SLH-DSA-SHA2-128f or SLH-DSA-SHA2-128s, pure mode, with the ctx domain "GUS2-TS"). The one-time nature of the underlying leaves MUST be enforced: a leaf that has signed once MUST never sign again; key trees SHOULD be rotated before exhaustion and the outgoing key SHOULD be archived for verification only, with the rotation anchored in the notary log. The reference implementation may use a WOTS16-Merkle-SHA256 educational scheme for vectors; it MUST NOT be used in production.

section.title: Daily notary
section.t: The notary chains the days: day_root(n) = SHA-256(L("GUS2-DAY") || u64be(n) || tree_root(n) || day_root(n-1)), where L applies a 4-byte big-endian length prefix to each part. Leaves are SHA-256(0x00 || payload) and internal nodes are SHA-256(0x01 || left || right); an odd trailing leaf is duplicated, and an empty day hashes to SHA-256("GUS2-EMPTY"). Days MUST be sealed in strict order (0, 1, 2, ...) and empty days MUST also be sealed, so no gap can be silently inflated. Each replica publishes its day roots independently; a consumer accepts a day when at least k of n replicas agree and each accepted root derives correctly. History editing is only invisible if the attacker rewrites every independent replica without any external observer noticing the divergence.

section.title: Conformance
section.t: The normative test vectors of GUS 2.1 are published as a machine-readable file (gus-normative-002.json) in the specification repository. An implementation is conforming if and only if it passes 100% of the categories of that file that it claims to support; the calendar, format and instant categories are mandatory for every implementation, and the signature/notary categories are mandatory for implementations that emit or verify GST. Implementations MUST consume the published vector file directly rather than copying vectors by hand.

At the time of writing, three independent implementations pass the core categories with zero divergence under differential fuzzing: the Python reference, the JavaScript (web) kernel, and an independent C implementation.

section.title: IANA Considerations
section.t: This document, if accepted, requests the following registrations.

section.title: Media type registration
section.t: Type name: application. Subtype name: gus-gst+json. Encoding: UTF-8 JSON. Security considerations: Section of this document. Interoperability: see the conformance clause. Applications that use this media type: signed timestamping of documents, API responses, logs. Publications: this specification. Person: verared. Intended usage: COMMON.

section.title: GUS Error Codes registry
section.t: A new registry "Gerarion Universal Standard Error Codes" with policy "Specification Required". The initial registry contains: GERO_EINVAL (malformed syntax or field out of range), GERO_ETEMPALUM (Tempalum day nonexistent for the year type), GERO_EWEEK (declared weekday letter inconsistent with the computed one, strict mode). New codes MUST be registered here and MUST NOT be assigned by implementers unilaterally.

section.title: GUS TCJ Offsets registry
section.t: The TCJ offset is an integer number of hours in the range -23..+23. A new registry "Gerarion Universal Standard TCJ Offsets" assigns semantic names to offsets. Initial entries: TCJ+0 (GUS reference offset, default), TCJ-7 (Example Zone). Offsets outside -23..+23 MUST be rejected with GERO_EINVAL. The registry is semantic, not computational: arithmetic never consumes the offset.

section.title: GUS Certification-Fork Epochs registry
section.t: A fork of GUS differs only in epoch constants (origin JDN and week offset); the algorithm is identical. A new registry "Gerarion Universal Standard Certification-Fork Epochs" with policy "Specification Required" records for each fork: mnemonic (short identifier, never a calendar-era claim), origin JDN, weekday offset, specification version, and status. The initial entry is "GUS" (origin JDN 1719313, weekday offset 0, this document). Certified forks MUST be verified against their own vector files derived by the same exact arithmetic.

section.title: Security Considerations
section.t: The threat model of GUS classifies attackers from individual hosts to coordinated notary capture; the full model, including the cost analysis (forgery of a current GST requires inverting the preimage resistance of SHA-256, on the order of 2^256 classical operations and at most a Grover speedup, or simultaneously rewriting every independent notary replica without external detection), is maintained in the specification repository (docs/spec/threat-model.md) and MUST be consulted for any deployment decision.

Implementations MUST NOT roll their own signature schemes for production: the reference hash-only scheme exists to generate and verify normative vectors, and production MUST use audited libraries of standardized schemes (FIPS 205 SLH-DSA, FIPS 204 ML-DSA, RFC 8554 LMS, RFC 8391 XMSS). One-time leaf discipline is mandatory and its violation is a catastrophic key disclosure. Verifiers MUST treat malformed input (including hostile JSON, absurd field lengths, and non-canonical whitespace) as invalid, never as a parser crash: the conformance and fuzzing suites include hostile-input vectors for exactly this reason.

section.title: Errata process
section.t: Corrections to this document follow the repository errata process: each errata entry carries an identifier (E-NN), the affected version, the erroneous text, the corrected fact or behavior, and the vector or test that demonstrates the correction. An errata that changes normative behavior requires a new vector set and a comment period before the next specification version. The corpus v1.2 errata (E-01 through E-07) are recorded in the specification repository.

section.title: IANA considerations for existing registrations
section.t: None. This document does not modify any existing IANA registry and does not require any immediate action; the registrations in the IANA Considerations section are requested for the standardization track.

section.title: Fundamental constants
section.artwork: ORIGIN_JDN = 1719313 (day index 0) SOLAR_DELTA_UD = 1242190 (microdays per common year excess) SOLAR_THRESHOLD_UD = 7000000 (Great Tempalum threshold, microdays) YEAR_COMMON_DAYS = 364 (52 weeks) YEAR_GRAN_DAYS = 371 (53 weeks) SECS_PER_DAY = 86400 (no leap seconds) GT year sequence = 5, 11, 16, 22, 28, 33, 39, 45, ... canonical context = "GUS2-TS" (GST domain separation)
